Buy a ticket and ride the train at Hibari Station
Buy a ticket at Hibari Station to Minato: say where you want to go, read the fare, use the ticket machine, ask for the platform, understand the announcement and behave well on the train.
Get to the station
Tell the station attendant where you want to go
Buy a ticket at the ticket machine
Check you have the right platform
Board the train and get to Minato Station
Hibari Station. Today you're taking the train to Minato Station to see the sea.
Hello. Can I help you?
I'd like to go to Minato Station.
I will go to Minato Station.
Minato Station, where?
Yes, Minato Station. Do you need a ticket? Saying "ikitai desu" (I want to go) is easier to understand.
Excuse me, please say "Minato eki e ikitai desu" (I want to go to Minato Station).
It's 320 yen to Minato Station. It takes about 20 minutes.
Did you get that? How much is it to Minato Station?
320 yen.
230 yen.
Could you say that once more, please?
It's 320 yen. Three, hundred, twen-ty. Please say it again.
Yes. 320 yen. Three hundred and twenty.
You buy tickets at that machine. First, put the money in. Then press the button for your destination.
You stand in front of the ticket machine. What do you do first?
First I put the money in.
First I press the button.
You press the button only after putting money in. Please put the money in first.
You put in a 500-yen coin and press the 「ミナト」 button. A ticket and 180 yen change come out.
Do you have any other questions?
Which platform is it?
Where is the train?
Where is the toilet?
The train to Minato is on platform 2. Next time, ask "nanbansen desu ka" (which platform?).
The toilet is over there. The train to Minato is on platform 2.
The train to Minato is on platform 2. Please go up the stairs.
Which platform is the train to Minato on?
Number 2.
Number 3.
Platform 3 goes the other way. The train to Minato is on platform 2.
The next train is at 10:15. Only 5 more minutes.
10:15. Thank you.
11:15, right?
What time is it?
It's 10:15, not 11. Only 5 more minutes.
You stand on the platform. An announcement plays: "The train for Minato will arrive at platform 2 shortly. For your safety, please stand behind the white line."
What did the announcement say? What will you do?
I step back behind the white line.
I stand right in front of the line.
I listen once more.
Danger! The train is coming in. 「お下がりください」 means please step back.
The announcement has ended. The train is about to arrive. Step back behind the white line.
The train is fairly empty. But at the next station, an elderly person gets on and stands in front of the priority seats.
You're sitting down. What do you do?
You say "douzo, suwatte kudasai" (please, have a seat).
You pretend to sleep.
You look down at your phone.
The elderly person says "Thank you. You're very kind" and smiles.
The elderly person looks a little tired. At the next station, someone else gives up their seat. Next time, try speaking up too.
You arrive at Minato Station. The doors open and the smell of the sea rushes in.
The last train home is at 11 p.m. Don't forget.
Summary: "~ tai desu" (I want to ~), "nanbansen desu ka" (which platform?), "mazu, sorekara" (first..., then...). At the station: stay behind the white line, and offer your seat to those who need it.
